penalties_applied.name: b2c_at_scale_needed
penalties_applied.reason: The buyer is individual consumers/knowledge workers — not a business role with a budget line. Monetizing a browser extension at meaningful revenue requires thousands of paying individual users.

rationale: The 'I would pay' signal is real but the buyer is individual consumers — knowledge workers and HN readers — who are historically reluctant to pay for browser extensions or feed filters beyond a one-time small fee. At the scale needed to generate meaningful revenue this is a B2C volume play, which conflicts directly with the factory's autonomy model. Critically, reliable AI-content detection is a genuinely hard technical problem: current classifiers (GPTZero, etc.) have high false-positive rates and providers actively game them, meaning the service would face constant accuracy complaints requiring human-judgement support and model retraining — neither of which can be delegated to Claude. The combination of a vague consumer buyer, a technically brittle core, and the scale needed to monetize makes this the wrong thing to build now.
solution_plan: Not recommended for build. If pursued: the factory could build a simple web-based text scorer (paste text → get AI-probability score) using an off-the-shelf detection API (Sapling, GPTZero) plus a Stripe paywall for a small monthly fee. A landing page + intake form + Stripe link is buildable in a week. However, the detection accuracy problem means users will immediately complain about false positives on human-written text, requiring ongoing human triage. There is no credible path to hands-off delivery here without solving a hard ML problem first. A solo non-technical operator cannot realistically maintain accuracy at a level customers will pay for.
notes: Fails buyer_clarity gate (score 3 < floor 6): buyer is vague consumers, not a specific business role. Fails operational_autonomy gate (score 5 < floor 7): AI detection accuracy requires ongoing human-judgement support. Also b2c_at_scale_needed penalty applied.
